answer: The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce. The design leans on random re-execution by unrelated peers, forfeited on duplicate submission, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Reaching the meadow of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short. The ferrous holds work receipts rather than names, so the anchor of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread.
